references.text: Moses fasted for forty days and forty nights when he received the tablets of the law on Mount Sinai, the same time period mentioned here.
Earlier in the same chapter, Moses describes his first forty-day fast on the mountain, to which this second fast refers back.
Moses repeats that he threw himself down before the Lord for forty days and forty nights and prayed for the people.
Moses summarizes his forty days and nights on the mountain when he prayed for the people, and the Lord heard his prayer.
Moses' intercession for the people after the sin of the golden calf, where he asks the Lord to turn away from His anger.
Elijah also fasted for forty days and forty nights when he went to God's mountain Horeb.
Jesus fasted for forty days and forty nights in the wilderness, parallel to Moses' fast.
Ezra fasted and mourned over the people's unfaithfulness and sin, similar to Moses' intercession for Israel's sin.
Daniel fasted, prayed, and confessed the people's sins, just like Moses' intercession.
